failure_modes.recovery: Use contact_upsert to merge into the existing row instead of creating a duplicate.
failure_modes.when: a contact with the same email (or the same phone) already exists in this tenant

failure_modes.recovery: Fix the named field and retry — the error carries the worked example.
failure_modes.when: a field is missing/over-length, status or source is outside its enum, tags is not a JSON array of strings, or a composite note/interaction child is malformed

preconditions: ONE CALL records the whole first touch: pass note (a string → first note) and/or interaction {type, summary, occurred_at?} (→ first activity, bumps freshness). Granular contact_note_create / interaction_create remain for later touches.
Phone is optional — never invent a placeholder. Dedupe runs on email OR phone.
tags is a JSON array of strings, e.g. ["supplier","penang"] (max 50 tags).
Dates (last_contact_at, interaction.occurred_at) accept "YYYY-MM-DD" (parsed server-side as UTC midnight) or epoch milliseconds.

description: Create a contact and, in the same call, log its first note and/or first interaction — the composite first-touch door. Children validate before the contact write; if the contact commits but a child then fails, the error names the contact's id plus the exact call to finish it, never a silent orphan. A contact with the same email or phone already in this tenant refuses with CONFLICT. NEXT: contact_upsert merges into an existing contact instead of creating a duplicate.

interaction.description: Log the first interaction in the same call: {type, summary, occurred_at?} — occurred_at takes "YYYY-MM-DD".

note.description: Log a first note in the SAME call — ONE call makes both.
